senses.definition: Letters or numbers that tell you where an item belongs in a library collection.
senses.example: I wrote down the call number before I went to find the book on its shelf.

senses.definition: A way one library borrows a book or other item from another library so a reader can use it.
senses.example: The librarian arranged an interlibrary loan for a book about local birds.

senses.definition: A version of something such as a book or picture that is kept in a form a computer can store or show.
senses.example: I read a digital copy of the old letter because the paper was too fragile to touch.

senses.definition: A process in which a computer looks at pictures of writing and works out which letters and words they show.
senses.example: Optical character recognition let me search an old newspaper for a name.

senses.definition: A small mark placed near a letter in some writing systems to show a vowel sound.
senses.example: The book for new readers showed the vowel point below the Hebrew letter.

senses.definition: A guide that describes a group of records and helps a person decide where to look in it.
senses.example: The finding aid showed which box held the letters from Boston.

senses.definition: A preserved example linked to the scientific name of a group of living things, often a species.
senses.example: A scientist compared the plant to the type specimen kept in a herbarium.

senses.definition: A copy made to match the shape of a fossil.
senses.example: The museum’s fossil cast showed the dinosaur’s sharp teeth in great detail.
